transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-09 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai (Redwood) — Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Ravi Patel (Ember Retail)

Summary (auto): Quick SDK walkthrough, auth patterns, console demo, next steps specified.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here, I'm the AE. Um, quick intro, Priya our solutions engineer will run the demo and codewalk.
00:12 Sofia: Hi all, Sofia here; thanks. We're really excited to see the SDKs — we've been looking at latency, cost tradeoffs.
00:20 Priya: Great, quick agenda, we'll do auth, env setup, Python quickstart, TypeScript quickstart, then console/Optimize tour and Q&A. Should be about 45 minutes.
00:35 Liam: Sounds good. We have folks from infra and engineering on the call so feel free to get into details.
01:05 Priya: Ok jumping in — auth first. Redwood supports api keys for server-to-server, and SSO for team-level access. Typical pattern is set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var, or use our sso token exchange if you want per-user audit logs.
01:28 Ravi: Quick q, do you integrate with our existing IdP? We use Okta.
01:33 Alex: Yes, SAML/OKTA supported — we have SSO + RBAC and can map groups. We'll send the SSO integration doc.
01:50 Priya: On local dev, we recommend a short-lived dev key. For production, use KMS-backed keys — Redwood integrates with AWS KMS and GCP KMS, also HSM on private deployments.
02:10 Sofia: Noted. Also curious about token rotation cadence best practices.
02:18 Priya: We recommend rotation every 30 days if you can. For Dedicated or Private you can enforce rotation through your KMS policies.
02:35 Alex: Quick pause — one thing I want to highlight, for PII/PCI scopes we usually recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering and audit logs.
02:52 Liam: That was our expectation. Ok.
03:10 Priya: Moving to environment setup. Typical env variables: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENDPOINT (for dedicated/private), REDWOOD_REGION. For local testing we provide a small mock server in the quickstart repo.
03:32 Priya: I'll share the link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart (note: placeholder link).
03:45 Ravi: Is there a Docker image for local dev?
03:50 Priya: Yep, a lightweight docker-compose with the mock runtime.
04:10 Priya: Now code, Python first.
04:20 Priya: "import redwood; client = redwood.Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))" then client.generate(...). The SDK hides streaming and handles reconnects.
04:45 Priya: Example snippet: response = client.chat.create(model='rw1-large', input='Summarize this order...') — note model names are in the catalog.
05:10 Sofia: Are models pinned per-route? We have many services that need stable model versions.
05:16 Priya: Yes you can pin model versions in route configs and we support rollouts/canaries.
05:35 Alex: (overlap) Also there's auto-fallback to smaller quantized variants if capacity is constrained.
05:45 Sofia: Ok good.
06:05 Priya: TypeScript/Node example: import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ model: 'rw1-large', messages: [...] });
06:30 Ravi: How does batching work with the SDK? We have a high QPS chat gateway and want to batch short prompts.
06:40 Priya: SDK has client-side batching helpers and server-side continuous batching. For high QPS we can tune batch size and latency targets. Optimize will also surface batching suggestions per-route.
07:05 Liam: Are there libraries for retry/backoff?
07:10 Priya: Yes built-in retries with exponential backoff, and you can plug in your own policy.
07:20 Priya: Ok switching to Console — I'll share screen (descriptive). In the Console you create a Route, attach model, set concurrency and SLOs, and view per-token cost and latency heatmaps.
07:45 Priya: Here's the route config area — you can pin model, set fallback variants, and configure KV cache for prefix caching.
08:10 Sofia: That KV cache, is it per-customer or shared?
08:16 Priya: It's per-route and can be isolated by customer id. For Private deployments you get customer-managed cache storage if needed.
08:35 Priya: Optimize tab — gives batching suggestions, quantization recommendations, and impact estimates on cost and latency. You can run a simulated workload against the optimizer.
08:55 Ravi: Does Optimize run real traffic or simulation?
09:00 Priya: It can do both. For simulation you upload representative payloads, and for live measurement we sample traffic with low overhead.
09:18 Liam: Are there SLAs around latency? We aim for p95 < 200ms for short responses.
09:25 Alex: For hosted API p95 depends on model/seq length — smaller models and quantized builds help; Dedicated can provide tighter SLOs. We'll include a latency profile doc.
09:45 Sofia: Speaking of cost, curious about unit economics vs OpenAI.
09:50 Alex: We often run competitive TCO analysis — can save 20-60% depending on batching and quantization. We'll include a sample TCO spreadsheet.
10:10 Sofia: Great.
10:30 Priya: Back to code: demonstration of streaming — client.chat.stream returns an async iterator in Python and an event emitter in Node. Streaming reduces perceived latency for end users.
10:55 Ravi: Ok that's important for chat.
11:10 Priya: Quick demo of TypeScript quickstart repo — show project layout, install instructions (npm i @redwood/inference), env file example.
11:35 Priya: Local run: NODE_ENV=development REDWOOD_API_KEY=devkey node examples/chat.js
11:50 Liam: Do you provide request/response logging hooks? We need to ship logs to Splunk.
11:58 Priya: Yes, SDK exposes hooks for request/response and we integrate with common logging sinks. For Private, full audit logs are available.
12:20 Sofia: What about data retention? We need retention controls on tokens.
12:28 Alex: You can configure retention per-account; Enterprise customers can opt for zero retention, or custom retention windows. Dedicated/Private give stricter controls.
12:50 Priya: Moving to POC scoping — what we need from you: expected QPS, payload sizes, sample prompts, target latency SLO, and security requirements.
13:10 Sofia: We'll get those over. Expected QPS is around 1200 sustained with peaks at 3500, average prompt ~150 tokens.
13:25 Priya: Great, that helps sizing. For that workload we'd recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscale and a couple of quantized variants.
13:45 Ravi: Any recommended quantization? We saw 4-bit profiles in your docs.
13:50 Priya: Yes 4-bit usually gives big cost wins for many workloads but check quality regressions with your evals — Optimize can run regression checks against prompt sets.
14:05 Liam: Ok. How long to stand up a Dedicated environment for a POC?
14:12 Alex: We can spin a trial Dedicated in 1-2 weeks depending on procurement, or start hosted with capacity reservations to get going faster.
14:28 Sofia: Procurement will prefer hosted to start then move to Dedicated.
14:40 Priya: We'll put together a recommended configuration and cost estimate.
15:00 Alex: Any other technical blockers?
15:05 Sofia: One last question — network egress and VPC peering for Private. Do you support cross-account peering?
15:12 Priya: Yes, Private offers VPC peering and customer-managed networking; we'll share network diagrams.
15:32 Alex: Alright quick recap of next steps: send pricing and Dedicated options, Priya share repos + docs, Ember share metrics. We'll follow up for POC scoping call.
15:50 Sofia: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
16:00 Liam: Thanks, look forward to the docs.
16:05 Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email.

(Transcript note: some ASR mislabels — "Redwood Dedicate" heard at 05:16 was "Redwood Dedicated"; proper noun spellings may vary in transcript.)
